name: New York Cares
description: New York Cares is one of the main volunteer networks in the city, connecting people to projects in education, food access, public spaces, and neighborhood support. It is a broad starting point if you want a lot of different NYC service options in one place.

name: New York Cares Youth Friendly
description: New York Cares’ Youth Friendly page is a starting point for younger volunteers looking for service projects that are more accessible to teens. It helps you find age-appropriate opportunities across the city without having to sift through the full project catalog.

name: New York Cares Project Search
description: This New York Cares search entry is aimed at volunteers looking for community opportunities in NYC. Use it to browse currently listed projects, check any age limits, and sign up for shifts that match your interests.

name: NYC Service Volunteer Search
description: This NYC Service listing points to the city’s volunteer search portal for citywide opportunities, with a focus on community work. It is useful for browsing current openings, filtering by cause area, and finding organizations that need help right now.

name: NYC Service Home
description: NYC Service is the city’s volunteer hub, where you can browse service opportunities across many neighborhoods and issue areas. It is best used as a starting point for finding active projects run by nonprofits, schools, and community groups.

name: NYC Parks Volunteer
description: NYC Parks’ volunteer page covers hands-on outdoor service across the five boroughs, including park cleanups, gardening, stewardship, and community events. It is a strong option for teens who want visible, local, in-person work.

name: City Harvest Volunteer
description: City Harvest’s volunteer page focuses on helping rescue and distribute food across New York City. It is especially appealing if you want hands-on service tied to hunger relief and food access.

name: God's Love We Deliver Volunteer
description: God’s Love We Deliver offers volunteer roles connected to preparing and delivering medically tailored meals. It is a meaningful option for students interested in food access and health-related community service.

name: Food Bank For NYC Volunteer
description: Lend a hand, pack a bag, serve a meal—your time helps New Yorkers thrive. Volunteer solo or with your team. Make real impact across the city.

name: Central Park Conservancy Volunteer
description: The Conservancy is the only organization that tends to the full care of Central Park. With 843 acres to manage, there’s a lot of ground for our volunteers…

name: Prospect Park Alliance Volunteer
description: Prospect Park Alliance offers volunteer opportunities tied to park care, restoration, and community events in Brooklyn. It works well for students who want outdoor service with a neighborhood feel.

name: GrowNYC Volunteer
description: GrowNYC’s volunteer work connects to sustainability, greenmarkets, composting, and food systems across the city. It is especially good for students interested in environmental service with a practical, everyday impact.

name: NYRR Volunteer
description: NYRR volunteers support races and running events throughout the city. It is a good fit for students who like energetic, event-based service and do not mind being part of a fast-moving public event.

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden Volunteer
description: Brooklyn Botanic Garden volunteers contribute many hours in almost every department throughout the Garden. Volunteer positions open periodically as needs arise.

name: Queens Botanical Garden Volunteer
description: Join the volunteers making a difference at our 39-acre outdoor urban oasis. Explore the many ways to get involved- get fresh air and your hands dirty with our knowledgeable Horticulture staff; assist visitors and children explore nature with Education and Public Programs; gain valuable technical skills in Maintenance; learn to turn Compost or tend to our Urban Farm; or share your Administrative and creative skills with our friendly staff.

name: Bronx River Alliance Volunteer
description: Bronx River Alliance’s volunteer opportunities center on river stewardship, cleanups, and community environmental work. It is a strong option for students who want hands-on outdoor service in the Bronx.

name: Staten Island Greenbelt Volunteer
description: The Staten Island Greenbelt volunteer page points to conservation and stewardship opportunities in a large network of parks and trails. It is a solid choice for students who enjoy outdoor, place-based service.

name: Habitat for Humanity NYC
description: Habitat for Humanity NYC offers volunteer opportunities connected to housing and neighborhood support. It is especially appealing if you want service that feels tied to long-term community rebuilding.

name: NYPL Volunteer
description: The New York Public Library volunteer page highlights ways to support library programs, outreach, and community learning. It is a good fit for students who like education-focused service in public spaces.

name: Queens Library Volunteer
description: Queens Public Library’s volunteer page is geared toward helping library programs and branch communities. It is a good option for students who want education-related service close to neighborhood life.

name: Brooklyn Public Library Volunteer
description: Want to enrich your own life and the lives of others? Spread the love of reading and learning, curiosity, and tolerance? Improve your local branch library? Join hundreds of volunteers who share their time, skills, and energy to strengthen the library community.

name: Bowery Mission Volunteer
description: The Bowery Mission offers volunteer opportunities related to meals, hospitality, and support services for people facing homelessness and poverty. It is a direct-service option with a clear human impact.

name: New York Common Pantry Volunteer
description: New York Common Pantry is dedicated to reducing hunger throughout New York City while promoting dignity and self-sufficiency.

name: Housing Works
description: Housing Works is a New York City based non-profit fighting the twin crises of AIDS and homelessness.

name: Covenant House New York
description: Covenant House New York supports young people facing homelessness and instability. This page is a starting point for learning about volunteering with an organization centered on youth support and shelter-related services.

name: Ali Forney Center
description: Ali Forney Center supports LGBTQ+ youth experiencing homelessness. This page is a starting point for learning about the organization and the kinds of support roles it may offer.

name: PAL NYC
description: PAL NYC connects young people to sports, mentoring, and youth development programs. It is a strong option for students who want service tied to younger kids, recreation, and education.

name: Met Council Volunteer
description: Met Council’s volunteer page points to hunger-relief and community-support work across New York. It is a good choice for students who want service connected to food distribution and social support.

name: Masbia
description: Masbia Soup Kitchen Network’s emergency food programs serve over 2 million meals a year in two main categories. We serve roughly 100,000 hot, sit-down dinners to clients at our restaurant like soup kitchens, and the rest in emergency care packages with the equivalent of 9 meals worth of groceries for every member of the family.

name: UJA Federation Volunteer
description: UJA-Federation’s volunteer page collects service opportunities connected to its network of community organizations. It is useful if you want a broad entry point into organized community service in New York.

name: JCC Manhattan Teens
description: JCC Manhattan’s teen page highlights youth programming, leadership, and community opportunities. It is a better fit for students looking for teen-centered engagement than for a single traditional volunteer shift.

name: 92NY Teens
description: 92NY’s teen page focuses on programs, arts, learning, and youth engagement. It is best for students looking for enrichment or leadership-style opportunities rather than one narrow volunteer role.

name: Wave Hill Volunteer
description: Wave Hill offers volunteer opportunities in a garden and cultural setting in the Bronx. It is a nice fit for students who like nature, education, and a quieter environmental atmosphere.

name: Volunteer New York Youth Opportunities
description: Volunteer New York Youth Volunteer Guidebook and Smartphone App

name: VolunteerMatch
description: VolunteerMatch is a large search platform for volunteer opportunities rather than one single program. It is helpful when you want to compare many listings and then click into a specific role.

name: VolunteerMatch Virtual Volunteering
description: This VolunteerMatch page highlights remote opportunities connected to community work. It functions more like a search platform than a single program, so the best use is browsing listings and then choosing a specific organization to apply to.

name: VolunteerMatch NYC
description: This VolunteerMatch page is geared toward finding volunteer roles in and around New York City. It is useful if you want to compare many organizations in one place and then click through to a specific listing.

name: Ali Forney Center Volunteer
description: Ali Forney Center’s volunteer page is the more direct route for people interested in supporting LGBTQ+ youth experiencing homelessness. It is useful if you want to explore concrete ways to help rather than just read about the organization.

name: Zooniverse
description: The Zooniverse is the world's largest and most popular platform for people-powered research.

name: Smithsonian Digital Volunteers
description: Smithsonian Digital Volunteers invites people to transcribe and review historical documents, field notes, and archival material online. It is a good fit for students who like research, history, and detail-oriented virtual work.

name: Library of Congress By the People
description: Crowdsourcing project By the People invites anyone to become a Library of Congress virtual volunteer. Explore, transcribe, review, and tag digital collections to improve search and readability and open new avenues of research.

name: Be My Eyes Volunteer
description: Experience the benefits of accessible technology with Be My Eyes. Connect with volunteers for real-time assistance via video.

name: Crisis Text Line Volunteer
description: Crisis Text Line trains remote volunteers to support people reaching out in moments of crisis by text. Because the role is more serious and training-based than most teen volunteering, it is worth reading the requirements carefully before applying.

name: Idealist Volunteer Search
description: Ready to make a difference? Search for internships at nonprofits and purpose-driven companies

name: Points of Light Engage
description: Points of Light Engage is a volunteer search platform that aggregates opportunities from many organizations. It is most useful as a place to browse and compare listings rather than as one standalone volunteer program.

name: Catchafire
description: Catchafire focuses on skills-based service projects, often helping nonprofits with professional or creative tasks. It is better suited to students who already have a skill they want to contribute, such as design, writing, or tech.

name: UN Volunteers
description: UN Volunteers is a global volunteering hub connected to international service and development work. It is more exploratory than local NYC volunteering, but it can help students discover larger-scale service pathways and virtual options.

name: Amnesty International Youth
description: This Amnesty International youth page is centered on human-rights activism and youth organizing. It fits students who are drawn to advocacy, campaigns, and issue-based action more than traditional hands-on volunteering.

name: UNICEF USA Clubs
description: UNICEF USA’s youth pages focus on clubs, campaigns, and service projects organized by students. It is a good option if you want structured advocacy and community work with a youth leadership angle.

name: Ocean Conservancy Action Center
description: Ocean Conservancy’s action page gathers campaigns and advocacy steps connected to ocean protection. It is best for students interested in environmental action and awareness work that can be done online.

name: WWF How to Help
description: WWF’s action page highlights ways supporters can get involved in conservation and environmental advocacy. It is more of an issue-action page than a traditional volunteer signup, but it still gives students a path into environmental engagement.

name: The Humane Society Action
description: The Humane Society Action is a virtual opportunity connected to animals and advocacy. Visit the website to see how participation works, what the expectations are, and whether the role fits your schedule.

name: Smithsonian Volunteer Info
description: Smithsonian Volunteer Info is a virtual opportunity connected to arts and research. Visit the website to see how participation works, what the expectations are, and whether the role fits your schedule.

name: SciStarter
description: SciStarter connects people to citizen science projects, citizen scientists, and resources. Real science we can do together.
